content:
Formula: Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) Conditions
Exact Expression: \nabla f(x^*) + \sum_{i=1}^m \mu_i \nabla g_i(x^*) + \sum_{j=1}^p \lambda_j \nabla h_j(x^*) = 0
Definitions: First-derivative necessary conditions for a solution in nonlinear programming to be optimal, provided regularity conditions hold.
Derivation/Reference: William Karush (MS thesis, 1939); Harold W. Kuhn & Albert W. Tucker (1951)
Example: Minimizing x^2 + y^2 subject to x + y >= 1 yields optimal x* = y* = 0.5 with multiplier mu = 1
Domain: optimization
Assumptions: Functions f, g_i, h_j are continuously differentiable; Constraint qualification (e.g. Slater's condition for convex problems)
Common Errors: Omitting dual feasibility requirement mu_i >= 0 for inequality constraints
